full_judgment:
2. The case of the plaintiffs is, inter alia, that the property described in the schedule to the plaint belonged to Durga Charan Prasanna Chakraborty and Ambika Chakraborty. The said 2 persons were the recorded tenants in SA Khatian. Ambika Chakraborty died leaving his brother Durga Charan Prasanna Chakraborty as the sole heir. Because of ailments Durga Charan Prasanna was bed ridden for long time and during that time his son Narayan Chakraborty was managing and looking after the property of his father Durga Charan Prasanna Chakraborty and at that time said Narayan Chakraborty sold 1.10 acres of land to plaintiff No. 1 (since deceased) and 2.04 acres of land to the plaintiff No. 2 on December 30, 1977 and made over possession of the land so transferred to them. It may be mentioned in the kabalas of the plaintiffs there has been recital that Narayan Chakraborty inherited the land from Durga Charan Prasanna Chakraborty and Ambika Chakraborty but in the Court it was the case of the plaintiffs that Narayan Chakraborty represented that he got the property by gift. Durga Charan Prasanna Chakraborty father of Narayan Chakraborty died on June 26, 1978. It is the specific case of the plaintiffs that Narayan Chakraborty on the death of Durga Charan Prasanna Chakraborty inherited his property and, as such, in view of the provision of sections 41 and 43 of the Transfer of Property Act plaintiffs have acquired right, title and interest in the land in suit. It is also the case of the plaintiffs that when they took steps for mutation of their names by filing Case No. 164 of 1980 at that time Narayan Chakraborty raised objection stating that he has sold 0.86½ acre of land to the defendant No. 1 by the kabala executed on March 10, 1979 and registered on March 18, 1979 and that he has also transferred 0.86½ acre of land to the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 by the kabala executed on March 12, 1979 and registered on March 14, 1979. Thereupon Mutation Case was rejected up to the appellate stage and thus the plaintiffs were constrained to file the suit. 

 3. The suit was contested by the defendant Nos. 1-3 stating, inter alia, that Narayan Chakraborty did not execute and register the kabalas in favour of the plaintiffs, that Narayan Chakraborty transferred the land which he inherited from his father to the defendants and that in the kabala of the defendant No. 1 as by mistake plot No. 470 was written in place of plot No. 370, Narayan Chakraborty executed and registered kabala rectifying the mistake. Similarly as by mistake in the kabala of defendant Nos. 2 and 3 Plot No. 470 was written in place of 370, Narayan Chakraborty executed and registered a rectification deed mentioning that he sold land of plot No. 370 and not land of plot No. 470, that the defendants by filing jama separation Case No. 465 of 1979-80 got their names recorded in the separate khatian No. 642 and paying rent, that the plaintiffs as against the order opening separate khatian in the name of the defendants filed appeal and therein they stated that Narayan Chakraborty sold land to them upon representing that he got the land by the registered deed of gift dated November 17, 1968 and Narayan Chakraborty upon entering appearance in the said appeal denied the execution and registration of the deeds in favour of the plaintiffs. It is the contention of the defendants that the deed of the plaintiffs are collusive, forged, fabricated and the same were never acted upon. 

 5. The learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that upon erroneous view of the provision of section 41 of Transfer of Property Act (the Act) as well as settled principle of law as regards purchase from ostensible owner High Court Division and the Court of appeal below were in serious error in holding that in the light of the provision of section 41 of the Transfer of Property Act plaintiffs have not acquired any title in the land purchased by them from Narayan Chakraborty in the year 1977. It may be mentioned appellate Court has reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court on the finding that plaintiffs by reliable evidence could not establish that Narayan Chakraborty transferred the land fraudulently or on false representation that he is otherwise owner of the property, nor the plaintiffs have established by reliable evidence that they were not aware of the fact that their vendor's (Narayan Chakraborty's) father, to whom the property belonged, at the material time i.e. in 1977, was alive. There are other material facts and one of those is that when the plaintiffs took steps for mutation of their names their vendor resisted the same denying transfer by him in favour of them. On the second occasion when the plaintiffs filed appeal as against the order opening separate khatian in the names of the contesting defendants, Narayan Chakraborty got himself impleaded in the appeal and denied the transfer in favour of the plaintiffs. In the background of the said conduct of Narayan Chakraborty the plaintiffs filed the suit without impleading him.
